transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. I'm here because... well, I just keep blowing up at people over nothing. I'm snapping at my team on operations calls, and I'm even doing it at home with my family. It's... it's getting really bad, and that is just not how I've ever handled things. I don't know why I'm acting like this, but I knew I needed to come in.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It's been about three weeks now. Basically... it started right after we had a valve failure at the facility. There was an injury when it happened, and I've just been acting like this ever since then.
Since that accident happened, do you find yourself having unwanted, vivid memories or nightmares about the event?

Yeah, I do. I can just be sitting at the kitchen table, or trying to answer emails from home, and... suddenly I’m right back there. I see the flash from that valve again, and the smoke in the aisle. It's like it just shoves everything else out of my head.
Since the accident, have you been going out of your way to avoid places, people, or activities that remind you of what happened?

No, I haven't really been doing that. I mean, I'm the manager, so I still have to go into the facility every day. I haven't been staying away from the plant or the guys on my team, or anything like that. I just... I still go where I need to go.
Aside from the irritability you mentioned, have you noticed any changes in your mood, such as feeling persistently down, numb, or detached from the people around you?

Yeah, I guess numb is a good way to put it. I just can't seem to feel good about things right now. Like, my wife will make dinner, or my kids will talk about soccer just like normal... and I know I should feel glad to be there with them. I want to. But it’s like there’s just nothing in me that can respond.
You mentioned the accident happened about three weeks ago; have you experienced these symptoms consistently for that entire three-week period, or have they been changing in intensity?

Yeah, it's been pretty consistent. It started right after the accident... ever since that valve failed and the guy got hurt. So, yeah, it's been the whole three weeks, just... going on like this without really letting up.
